candidates.source_title: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Christina Hartley and Roy Kitcher say the flats are "home" and they do not want to move Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision. Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said. Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns. Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option. Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home. "This is home and I want to stay here, I don't want to be moving out again," Kitcher added.
candidates.source_summary: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight".

candidates.source_title: Organised crime gang ‘manager’ jailed for supplying class-A drugs - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who played a significant role in an organised crime group which supplied class A drugs across Rochdale has been jailed for 10 years and six months. An investigation into Haider Ali was launched following information received that a drug deal had taken place from a car parked in Baron Street, in Rochdale town centre, just before midnight on January 4, 2025. Officers began to follow the vehicle and when it came to a stop at a local petrol station, officers immediately executed a reinforced stop to prevent it from making off. Ali, who was travelling as a passenger, exited the vehicle and began to speedily walk away before officers detained him. Following searches, Ali was found to be in possession of more than £1,000 in cash, and two mobile phones, all of which were seized. Ali was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class A drugs and taken to custody where further searches recovered two bundles of several wraps of a brown and a white substance. Tests later confirmed these substances to be heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid mobile phone seized from Ali was confirmed to be the Adam drug line. Following this, investigators also uncovered that Ali was not only dealing drugs at street level, but he was also managing other street dealers. Evidence suggested that Ali had progressed from being a street dealer in 2014 to holding a significant role within the Adam OCG in 2024 into 2025, managing street dealers and the dedicated dealer phone, and directing those below him on where there next deal is.

candidates.source_title: 'A sad day for College Bank and for Rochdale' as Seven Sisters to be demolished
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Residents of the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale have been left saddened, angered and disappointed after learning their homes are going to be bulldozed. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) have made the decision to demolish the 766 flats and replace them with a mix of 601 new flats and townhouses. The decision brings to an end an era of uncertainty for the towers, actually called College Bank, which were first earmarked for demolition a decade ago. What used to be a bustling community on the outskirts of Rochdale town centre now sits silent. That’s because only around 80 households remain from the original 766 since the original demolition announcement 10 years ago. Even hardened campaigners from the Save the Seven Sisters (ST7S) group have gone. The campaigners have fought to stop demolition ever since it was first mentioned in 2016. They want to see the 1960s block refurbished instead. RBH deemed it too expensive and believed it would take too long to refurbish the blocks, so opted to redevelop. They estimated that it would take 12 years to refurbish and cost £269m – around £388,000 per flat. Then, even after that, homes would have an expected lifespan of around 50 years, according to RBH. Joan Wainwright was lost for words when she read RBH’s letter outlining their plan. She is angry. Joan owns her flat in Town Mill Brow, so is in a different position to other tenants who would need to be offered new accommodation by the social housing landlord. RBH have said previously they are offering to buy out leaseholders and vowed to support them in their move. “Here we go again,” the 72-year-old said. “We’re not playing. Just no. “There are too many anomalies with what they are saying and what they’re doing. They’re quoting figures that are totally off the planet. “Whatever they’re going to put in their place is going to be totally inferior. “We’ve had offers to buy, but they’re offering peanuts. The size of these flats are the equivalent of a terraced house. What they’re offering wouldn’t buy a terraced house. “As far as I’m concerned I am too old. At 72 why should I have to go property hunting. Thinking about selling all my furniture, which I’m not prepared to do, and starting all over again – no. “I moved in here when I was 36 and then 10 years later I bought it. I thought this is it – I’ve got the hospitals, I’ve got the shops – if I need a wheelchair I just need a little ramp and the flat is big enough. “Then someone thinks they’re going to pull the rug out. I don’t think so.” The decision has been made by landowners RBH after more than a year of working together with partners in the College Bank Task Force – which includes the council and Greater Manchester Combined Authority. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Businesses and individuals from across Rochdale borough have been recognised at the 13th annual Rochdale Business Awards. The awards recognise achievements ranging from business growth and customer service to sustainability, community engagement and the development of the next generation of Rochdale talent. The winners of 12 categories from Apprentice of the Year to Business of the Year were announced during the ceremony at Rochdale Town Hall on Friday. Wheeldon Bros Waste Ltd won Sustainable Environmental Business of the Year, while Performance Doorset Solutions Ltd took Business of the Year for turnover over £5m. Conor Weldon, of Salt Separation Services Ltd, was named Apprentice of the Year, and the company also won Employer of the Year. ALF Recruit won two awards, as New Business of the Year and Business of the Year for turnover under £1m. Cllr Neil Emmott, Leader of Rochdale Council, said: “Rochdale has a thriving and ambitious business community, with organisations across the borough creating jobs, investing in our towns and bringing new ideas and opportunities. The Business Awards are a fantastic opportunity to recognise the people and businesses driving that success. “From major developments at Kingsway and the reopening of Heywood Civic to the growing profile of our towns as places to live, work and visit, there is plenty of positive momentum across the borough. Supporting businesses to grow and recognising their contribution is an important part of that.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: This is what a new fire station for Heywood could look like. If approved, crews will operate from a temporary base on the site until the new station is complete. Plans for the temporary base were approved by the council in August. The new plans include two vehicle bays with accommodation, a community meeting room, drill yard and training facilities, including a four-storey training tower. The site has been designed to enable fire engines to enter the station from the rear and exit from the front to avoid vehicles reversing on to the site from Middleton. It is one of five ageing fire stations the service has identified for upgrade, including Whitefield, King Street and Whitehill in Stockport, and Blackley, which has recently been completed. candidates.source_title: Today marks 215 years since the birth of the 'greatest master of English oratory' John Bright, influential Rochdale-born statesman
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Today marks the 215th anniversary of the birth of the free-trade advocate and abolitionist John Bright (1811-1889). Celebrated and lauded by many, including Abraham Lincoln and Lord Salisbury, John Bright is arguably Rochdale's greatest statesman John Bright was a statesman from Rochdale, belonging initially to the Radical Party until its merger into the Liberal Party in 1859. He was lauded by many, Lord Salisbury, former Prime Minister three times over, upon Bright's death, remarked that "he (Bright) was the greatest master of English oratory that this generation has produced, or I may perhaps say several generations back." Abraham Lincoln had a portrait of John Bright in his office, and among the items retrieved from his pocket upon his assassination, was a testimony from Bright supporting the re-election of the President. Bright became an MP for 4 separate constituencies, and served as a cabinet minister on three separate occasions, all under Liberal Prime Minister William Gladstone. Bright was an abolitionist, and supported fugitive slave Frederick Douglass both spread his story, and become a free man. Bright was a supporter of the co-operative movement, and introduced Douglass to crowds almost a thousand strong in Rochdale wanting to hear him speak of his story as a slave in America. Frederick Douglass notably spoke in the Public Room on Baillie Street on October 10th 1846, just a three minute walk from where the first co-operative store was opened by the Rochdale Pioneers two years prior. Bright contributed a third of the cost to buy Douglass' freedom from slavery, and, in 1847, Douglass went back to America a free man. Douglass was a regular guest at 'One Ash', the home of John Bright, and he stayed there the night before he was to leave England for America as a free man for the first time. Douglass noted that, relating to the hospitality of Bright “I was, besides, a welcome guest at the home of Mr. Bright in Rochdale and treated as a friend and brother among his brothers and sisters.” Douglass went on to become an influential abolitionist and supporter of women's suffrage, being the only black attendant to the first women's rights convention, and the first black candidate for the vice-presidency under the first female candidate for the presidency. Bright was known for his staunch advocacy for free-trade policies, evidenced through his role in the Anti-Corn Law League, which he founded alongside his friend (and later MP for Rochdale) Richard Cobden. The Corn Laws were a set of mercantilist/protectionist tariffs and trade restrictions levied on imported wheat in an attempt to protect national farming interests. This caused the prices for common wheat products like bread to rise, disproportionately negatively impacting the urban working class. Bright joined forces with Cobden with the creation of one of the first nationwide successful pressure groups, officially in 1836, but functionally in 1838. In 1846, the Conservative Prime Minister Robert Peel led the successful battle for repeal, and the success of the pressure group established by Bright and Cobden was a primary reason for the eventual repealing of these laws, symbolising a shift in policy from mercantilism/protectionism to free trade. This was incredibly controversial, and the conservatives broadly didn't support this, with Peel relying on the support of the Whigs to pass the repeal of the Corn Laws. Peel resigned the very day that the repeal passed through parliament. Critics of the repeal of the Corn Laws, including Benjamin Disraeli, saw that the repeal of these laws caused the ruin of British agriculture, yet supporters of the repeal of these laws saw that the urban working class were baring an unfair load as a result of the expensive food prices. Benjamin Disraeli opted not to reinstate the Corn Laws for this reason, seeing the value of free-trade policies and the benefit that the repeal of the law had on the urban working class. Rochdale statesman John Bright, and former Rochdale MP Richard Cobden were two of the main pioneers for the repeal of the Corn Laws, and of the extension of free-trade policies in Britain. Two famous terms have been attributed to Bright, one being the idiom to 'flog a dead horse', and the other being in relation to England being the 'mother of all parliaments'. Bright has two statues, one near Manchester Town Hall, and the other in Broadfield Park in Rochdale. They were both unveiled in 1891, but the latter was moved from the initial placing of the Town Hall Square to the park in 1933. The inscriptions on the statue in Broadfield Park note Bright as 'Rochdale's greatest townsman', accompanied by quotes from the 'master of English oratory'.

candidates.source_title: Homeless support steps up as winter sweeps in – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_body_excerpt: People experiencing homelessness across Rochdale borough are being provided with extra support as the cold weather sweeps in. Temperatures are closely monitored and, when severe weather conditions are forecast, the support already available to people sleeping rough significantly increases across all townships. Additional outreach workers are now on the streets during the day and throughout the night, engaging with anyone sleeping rough and helping them access accommodation and support services. Bed capacity across accommodation services has been increased, while community support hubs will extend their opening hours during periods of severe weather. The hubs provide access to hot food and drinks, shower and laundry facilities, welfare support, health services and more to help people move away from rough sleeping and into longer-term accommodation. In addition, housing staff will continue to link in with the new Safe Haven site in Rochdale Town Hall Square. The Safe Haven is a trailer which parks in this area every Saturday between 10pm and 3am and is fully staffed with clinical and non-clinical teams to support anyone who is on a night out and feeling vulnerable. The teams supporting the homeless, including the council and its many partners, will continue to work with the safe haven team to ensure that anyone who is going into the haven because they need a bed for the night will be supported into accommodation. Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for housing and regeneration, said: “Council teams and partners work all year round to support our most vulnerable residents, but we know they are more at risk in cold weather. By significantly stepping up the support at this time of year, we will ensure that nobody who wants a bed will be without one. “This 24-hour response supports people in immediate crisis and that’s really important, but we also offer long term support because ultimately, we want people to be able to build a life away from the streets. As well as provision to help the person, like support with jobs, training and mental health, we’re also creating new move-on accommodation to help people who are working towards a permanent home, and in the longer term are working to create more affordable housing.”

candidates.source_title: There are ‘serious failings’ in how Bury council manages its social housing, a government watchdog has warned
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Outcomes in safety and accountability were judged to be particularly poor, with the Regulator of Social Housing saying it cannot be sure the town hall is meeting its legal duties. The council owns around 7,600 homes with some 300 of these managed by an external agency. It was the council’s first inspection under the regulatory framework and it was awarded a C3 rating – the second lowest outcome. The council took its housing services back into direct management in 2024 as it began to wind down social housing provider Six Town Housing (STH). It is in the process of consulting on the future of the remaining around 100 homes managed by STH, with a recent report recommending that these too be brought under the council control. The council believes that will offer ‘greater long-term stability’ for tenants, with alternatives being to sell them on. Among the concerns raised by inspectors were overdue fire safety remedial actions, with 2,800 outstanding at the time of the inspection. While most were assessed as being low to medium risk, the Regulator of Social Housing said there was a ‘lack of clarity’ about the time taken to complete them. The council also could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould. Awaab’s Law came into effect in October 2025, named in memory of two-year-old boy Awaab Ishak, who tragically died in 2020. Awaab died after prolonged exposure to mould in his Rochdale flat. The new law requires social housing landlords to investigate hazard reports, including of mould, within 10 working days. If the issue is judged to be a ‘significant hazard’, safety work must be completed within five working days, or 24 hours for an ’emergency hazard’. Any further work required must be carried out within a ‘reasonable’ time.

candidates.source_title: Ollie Pearce goal secures maximum points for York at Rochdale - Wilts and Gloucestershire Standard
candidates.source_body_excerpt: York City tasted victory on the ground where they secured promotion from the National League last season as Ollie Pearce’s goal gave them a 1-0 win at the Crown Oil Arena. Rochdale started brightly, with Dajaune Brown’s header cleared off the line by Harry Boyes six minutes in. On the stroke of half-time, Glenn Middleton was presented with a one-on-one opportunity only for York goalkeeper Alfie McNally to read his attempted dink finish and collect the ball comfortably. In between, the Minstermen had the better of the opening 45 minutes as Hiram Boateng’s effort deflected narrowly wide and Alex Hunt’s rising drive from 20 yards thumped an upright. McNally had to scramble across his goalline to save Brown’s 50th-minute header, and within five minutes the visitors had the lead when Pearce pounced and diverted the ball beyond Sam Waller and into the net. Aden Flint saw an 80th-minute header cleared off the line as Rochdale threatened an equaliser before McNally denied Ian Henderson and Ryan East as York resisted late home pressure.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale 0-1 York: City clinch first away win of the season to defeat old foes - The York Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: York City ended their long wait for a first away win of the season as a single goal separated the Minstermen and old title foes Rochdale. York’s last league win away from the LNER Community Stadium came at Tamworth in April, almost seven months ago. Returning to the stadium where City lifted the National League title 203 days ago, it was a reunion that Scott Lindsey’s side took in their stride to clinch a sixth win of their League Two campaign. Josh Stones might have been the hero in Rochdale last April, but it was strike partner Ollie Pearce that took the plaudits on Saturday as he bagged the only goal. Having come close in the first-half, striking the post, he got his reward in the second when flicking Ollie Banks’ low cross past Sam Waller. Rochdale had chances of their own, and having controlled the final 20 minutes, City’s defensive qualities were put to the test. Ryan Fallowfield had to make two goalline clearances, one in the first-half and another in the second, while Alfie McNally thwarted Ian Henderson in the final five minutes. But the Minstermen held on – with head coach Lindsey ending a barren run on the road that had been lingering over his career with York to date.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A hard-hitting warning has been issued about the dangers of illegal e-bikes and e-scooters as Christmas approaches. Greater Manchester Police and its partners are urging families to think carefully before buying off-road bikes, illegal e-bikes and e-scooters as Christmas gifts, warning that vehicles used unlawfully could be seized and destroyed — or lead to tragedy. One family which knows the devastating consequences they can cause is that of Jacob Calland, who died after being hit by a car while he was a passenger on an e-scooter when it went through a red light in Wythenshawe in March this year. He died from his injuries eight days later. Jacob’s mother, Carly Calland, said: “No words will ever be able to describe the pain caused by Jacob’s death. My heart has been smashed into a thousand pieces and there is nothing that can be done to fix it. My life is a living nightmare. “I climbed into the hospital bed to cuddle him and I fell asleep holding him. When I woke up, it was time to turn off the machines. I told Jacob I loved him just before he passed away. My baby boy was gone forever. “He won’t sit his GCSEs, he won’t have his sweet sixteen birthday party, he won’t go to his school prom. He won’t be able to follow his dreams. He won’t get married and won’t have children. His life ended the moment that collision happened.” The e-scooter rider, who was 14 at the time, received an 18-month youth referral order and a five-year driving ban after pleading guilty to causing death by dangerous driving, causing death by driving unlicensed, and causing death by driving uninsured.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Scott Lindsey plans to use York City’s history at Rochdale as motivation to end the Minstermen’s wait for a win on the road. York head to Rochdale this afternoon looking to claim a first away win of the season, having so far recorded three draws and four defeats from their seven matches on the road. The Crown Oil Arena is familiar territory for a lot of the travelling City squad, who produced an all-timer of a finale in the National League last season. Mani Dieseruvwe headed home what looked like the winner for Rochdale in the 96th minute, breaking hearts in the away stand. But with virtually the last kick of the game, striker Josh Stones scored the equalising goal that landed York their place in the Football League. Lindsey might not have been with the club on that day, but he intends to use it as fuel to end City’s away day hoodoo. “It’s the biggest thing for us, that’s all we want to do – win,” Lindsey assured.

candidates.source_title: Residents praised for Remembrance tributes - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thousands of people across the borough gathered to honour the nation’s war heroes and pay their respects to those who have made sacrifices in defence of the country, with commemorations taking place on Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day on Wednesday. Representatives from the Navy, Army and Royal Air Force joined veterans and civic dignitaries for parades and services in Rochdale town centre, Castleton, Heywood, Littleborough, Middleton, Norden, Milnrow and Wardle. Residents gathered as memorials fell silent, with the Last Post played at each service. Each included the immemorial words from Laurence Binyon’s 1914 poem, For the Fallen: “They shall grow not old as we that are left grow old; Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn; at the going down of the sun and in the morning. We will remember them.” Praising the tributes, Mayor of Rochdale Cllr Faisal Rana, said: “The turnout across the borough was incredible, as people of all ages gathered at memorials in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale to pay their respects. “On a poignant and moving Remembrance Day, we honoured the fallen, people of all faiths and no faith, from countries all over the world. It was a day when the whole community fell silent to reflect and remember. candidates.source_title: Rochdale AFC v York City: Minstermen chase fresh Spotland milestone with 'caged lion' desperate to feature - Yorkshire Post
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Some 204 days will have elapsed between the Minstermen's two visits there in 2026. Saturday's appointment will create nothing like the incredulous theatre of events on April 25, but the hope among the York contingent is that it produces another milestone moment, nevertheless. Back in late spring, York ended their decade-long absence from the Football League in the most scarcely-believable stoppage-time finale ever. On this occasion, the wait for the Minstermen revolves around securing their maiden away victory as an EFL club once again. Their last win on the road as a league club was back in September 2015. Scott Lindsey wasn't present in Lancashire, last time out, but he stressed that those astonishing scenes will form part of his pre-match preparations, as the majority of York players are still at the club. The York chief said: "I think it's important that the players feel that environment when they turn up at the stadium again. I can't comment on that because I obviously wasn't here then. "But all that they will remember are good memories from that stadium. And I think that is important. So we'll definitely be leaning on that. "I think it's important that we do mention it. "But it's for the players to remember those memories. It can only be a good thing that the last time they were there, what happened." The hero last time out was Josh Stones, whose 103rd-minute goal sparked ecstatic scenes among York's 1,500-following and 4,000-odd watching the beam-back at the LNER Community Stadium. Stones had done it tough since and is being integrated back into the first-team following a lumbar glute injury. Suffice to say, he is desperate to be involved at Dale. Lindsey added: "It's like caging a lion, isn't it? He'll be coming out of the traps ready to go again. "I think he showed some frustration in the fact that he didn't play in the Bradford game. He wanted to play, which is great. I want players who want to play, which is fantastic. "But we have to be really mindful of his load, bearing in mind he's been out for so long. And hopefully we get a fresher Josh Stones who can come on the pitch on Saturday and make a real impact. "And the more we do that, the closer we're getting to him to be a starter for us."

candidates.source_title: Ollie Banks ready to end away day dip as York City head to old foes Rochdale - The York Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ollie Banks assured there were no concerns in the dressing room with York City’s away form – but wants nothing more than to end their winless run on the road this Saturday. Banks was a part of the York squad that embarked on an incredible 18 match unbeaten run away from home in the National League last season, as City went on to clinch the title. But since promotion to League Two, it’s been much more of a challenge for the Minstermen to find wins away from the LNER Community Stadium. With three draws and four defeats from City’s seven matches on the road, only 17th-placed Bristol Rovers and 19th-placed Port Vale have worse records away from home. City have the chance to rectify that record when travelling to old foes Rochdale this Saturday, with Banks keen to play his part in rewarding the visiting supporters. “In the group, in our meetings and in training when we’re going into an away game, there’s nothing really surrounding it that worries us,” Banks told The Press. “I think in a lot of the games away from home, we’ve probably deserved a win. “There’s been a couple where we haven’t been at it, but we definitely should have had at least two or three wins away from home.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: York City travel to Rochdale tomorrow (Saturday) for their Sky Bet League Two fixture, with kick-off at 3pm. The Minstermen are looking to record their first away victory of the 2026/27 season. The game takes York back to a ground that holds special memories. York went out of the Jersey Mike’s Trophy after a defeat at Bradford City. Before that, they beat Northampton Town 4-0 in the FA Cup. In all-time head-to-head meetings, York just edge Rochdale, with 51 wins to Rochdale’s 46.

candidates.source_title: New lease of life for vacant town centre offices - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An office building which has been empty for almost a decade is being turned into flats. Alam Investments has been granted planning permission by Rochdale Council to turn the former office building at St James Place, 168 Yorkshire Street, in Rochdale town centre, into 21 self-contained apartments. The redevelopment of the three-storey building will include a mix of 17 one-bedroom flats and four two-bedroom flats. Planning documents submitted with the application state: “The building has been vacant for approximately eight years and is in need of investment and reuse. “The proposed scheme will bring the property back into productive use, provide much-needed housing in a sustainable location, and contribute positively to the vitality and regeneration of Rochdale town centre. “The property lies adjacent to notable heritage assets, including St Mary’s Ukrainian Catholic Church (Grade II listed), and is surrounded by a mix of commercial and residential uses. “In terms of heritage value, the building itself is of limited architectural and historic significance, lacking distinctive features of merit. Its primary contribution to the conservation area arises from its form, scale, and materiality, which ensure a degree of consistency within the surrounding townscape. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Microsoft 365 disruption has prompted Rochdale-based award-winning IT provider, No Fuss IT, to encourage businesses to look beyond everyday technical support and consider how they would keep communicating if their usual email service became unavailable. No Fuss IT, whose IT team is led by Finn O’Loughlin, provides email continuity as part of its enhanced approach to proactively supporting businesses, including organisations working towards or maintaining ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 requirements. When email stops working, the consequences can reach much further than an empty inbox. Customer enquiries can go unanswered. Purchase orders can be delayed. Staff can lose access to conversations they need to complete their work, while managers spend time finding out what is happening and deciding what to do next. For businesses affected by the latest Microsoft disruption over the last 24 hours, it raises a practical question. If the main route into your email becomes unavailable, have you got another way through? Think of it like a motorway with an alternative toll road. Most days, the motorway gets everyone where they need to go. It is familiar, convenient and part of the daily routine. But when a major incident closes the carriageway, everyone relying on that same route can find themselves stuck. Knowing that someone is working to reopen it does little to move the queue.

candidates.source_title: How Rochdale residents helped deliver 10,000 toys to 3,000 children as 2026 Christmas appeal launches - InYourArea
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council’s staff-run charity is collecting new, unwrapped gifts across more than 40 drop-off points ahead of Friday, December 11 Rochdale Borough Council’s staff-run charity, Number One Riverside Giving Back, is now collecting donations for this year’s Christmas Toy Appeal. The annual campaign helps ensure children living in poverty across the borough have presents to open on Friday, December 25. Organised by council staff for the past 13 years, the appeal is accepting donations at borough libraries and Your Trust leisure centres until Friday, December 11. Last year, volunteers distributed a record 10,000 toys to around 3,000 children, building on a programme that has brought festive cheer to thousands of youngsters since 2013. Council policy advisor Helen Walton, from the Giving Back charity, said: “Christmas should be a magical time for every child, but for many families the financial pressures they face mean that even a small gift can feel impossible to afford. We’re already seeing requests for help, and that’s why every donation matters. "Knowing there’s something to unwrap on Christmas morning will mean the world to a child. We’re incredibly grateful for the continued kindness of our communities, whose support helps bring joy and hope to families when they need it most.” To take part, supporters simply need to donate a new, unwrapped gift suitable for a child or teenager up to age 16. Alongside libraries and leisure centres, collection points are open at the first-floor management office at Rochdale Riverside, The Trade Centre UK at Sandbrook Park, and The Old Police Station in Heywood. A full list of more than 40 drop-off locations and alternative ways to support the campaign is available at rochdale.gov.uk/ChristmasToyAppeal . Organisers are also encouraging residents to shop sustainably within the borough where possible, though every donation is warmly welcomed regardless of size. Supporters who prefer to shop online can have gifts delivered directly to Giving Back - Christmas Toy Appeal, Rochdale Borough Council, Number One Riverside, Smith Street, Rochdale OL16 1XU. All postal deliveries must arrive by Friday, December 11, so volunteers have time to sort and distribute them before Christmas Day.
